title: The persuasion treated here is reflex, secondary, for faith’s perfection—not justification’s instrument
source_text: XXIX. Itaque illa de qua agimus persuasio, fidei quidem actus est, sed reflexus, non directus; non primarius, sed secundarius. Nec ad fidei essentiam, sed ad perfectionem ejus solum pertinet. Prior ille est quo justificamur, cuique promittitur salus, & peccatorum remissio. Alter vero non item. Hic enim posterior, ut jam diximus, praesupponit fidem, tanquam in nobis ante existentem, & justificationem, ut jam factam sequitur: ac proinde in eo ipso fidei natura & essentia consistere nequit, sed quidam ejus est fructus & complementum. Nec potest esse justificationis conditio, sive causa instrumentalis; sed solum quidam ejus sensus & apprehensio.
pass_a_gloss: And so the persuasion of which we are treating is indeed an act of faith, but reflex, not direct; not primary, but secondary. It pertains not to the essence of faith but only to its perfection. The former is that by which we are justified, and to which salvation and remission of sins are promised. The latter is not so. For this posterior act, as we have already said, presupposes faith as already existing in us, and follows justification as already made: and therefore the nature and essence of faith cannot consist in it itself, but it is a certain fruit and complement of it. Nor can it be the condition or instrumental cause of justification; but only a certain sense and apprehension of it.
pass_b_english: Assurance is a reflex secondary act for faith’s perfection, not its essence.
It follows justification already made and cannot be justification’s instrumental condition.
